talks.title: How to talk to the Wish Machine?
talks.venue: Harnessing Quantum 2026, online invited lecture (40 min).
talks.abstract: Abstract. Why do seemingly all-powerful wish machines so often cause trouble in fiction and myth? They misinterpret human intentions and fulfill wishes in unexpected ways. Similar failures arise in AI-driven scientific research: systems may optimize the wrong objective, exploit a benchmark, or rely on an outdated proxy. Avoiding them requires learning how to communicate with the "wish machine" in the right language. In this talk, I will share practical lessons from developing algorithms for quantum many-body systems and discuss how AI may reshape future algorithm design.

research: I develop variational iMPS methods that sum algebraically decaying interactions directly through transfer-matrix functions. This connects numerical linear algebra and stable differentiation to the study of long-range quantum systems and criticality.

I develop scalable iPEPS contraction and optimization algorithms, including QR-based CTMRG and preconditioning, and use them to study frustrated magnets, spin liquids, and the interplay of topological and symmetry-breaking orders.
